title: Make dashboard worker execution and pipeline activity observable

output.summary: Make the trace-first dashboard reliable, narrate pipeline progress, and expose bounded worker diagnostics beneath one authoritative Implementation Loop.

approvedChanges.question: CHG-dashboard-reliable-session-observability
approvedChanges.currentState: Dashboard can leave an unexplained static shell when serving lifecycle fails; /reload may retain imported package modules and /wiki-dashboard may return stale endpoint metadata without proving state is served.
approvedChanges.desiredState: Preserve current Sprints Queue and Trace Detail. Health-check returned endpoints, distinguish loaded and installed runtime identity, require full restart when needed, clean stale metadata, and show loading/live/reconnecting/stale/failed plus last successful update.
approvedChanges.rationale: Observability must expose its own health and freshness.
approvedChanges.maintainerImpact: Lifecycle and activation become explicit contracts.
approvedChanges.routeRationale: Crosses lifecycle, protocol, browser, tests, and docs.
approvedChanges.expectedBehavior: Healthy sessions return populated verified endpoints; unhealthy sessions return exact remediation, never false success.
approvedChanges.regressionPlan: Real Pi process and browser tests cover startup, endpoint, reload, mismatch, restart, shutdown, cleanup, loading, loss, recovery, and failure.
approvedChanges.safetyBoundary: Loopback dashboard serving lifecycle, token capability, pinned-runtime identity, and read-only API availability.
failureModes: browser transport loss without visible recovery
approvedChanges.negativeTestPlan: Prove dead ports, stale tokens, mismatched loaded identity, failed restart, disconnected SSE, unavailable state, and shutdown all fail visibly and safely.
approvedChanges.compatibilityImpact: Existing Sprints Queue, Trace Detail, URL capability, and read-only APIs remain; only unhealthy starts change from false-success URL to actionable failure.

approvedChanges.question: CHG-implementation-worker-observability
approvedChanges.currentState: One trace-level Implementation Loop owns aggregate quality, but users cannot understand each worker's Task execution or how parallel results converge.
approvedChanges.desiredState: Keep one Implementation Loop per Sprint Trace. Show workers as Task Assignment attempts with local evidence; retain trace-level authority for coverage, conflicts, aggregate acceptance, quality, and merged proof. Extend only Implementation Trace Detail with worker lanes and Integration and Exit Review.
approvedChanges.rationale: Concurrent execution needs visibility without multiple semantic authorities.
approvedChanges.userImpact: Users understand worker progress and aggregate blockers.
approvedChanges.routeRationale: Coordinates runtime, projection, UI, tests, and docs.
approvedChanges.expectedBehavior: Worker attempts converge visibly into aggregate review; direct work renders without fake workers.
approvedChanges.regressionPlan: Cover worker lifecycle, retries, conflicts, partial collection, direct implementation, and every aggregate exit status.
approvedChanges.currentPain: Current detail cannot explain worker Task, activity, checks, acceptance coverage, paths, blocker, lease, retry, or convergence.
approvedChanges.desiredOutcome: Users can follow every worker attempt and aggregate validation while one Implementation Loop remains authoritative.
approvedChanges.successSignal: Fixture and browser coverage proves direct and worker implementations across queued/running/stale/blocked/failed/completed/retried/conflicting and aggregate exit states.
nonGoals: no worker authority to close Implementation
no redesign outside Implementation Trace Detail

approvedChanges.question: CHG-worker-observation-signal-boundary
approvedChanges.currentState: Durable worker lifecycle is too sparse for live activity, while copying raw prompts, reasoning, tools, and logs into traces would be unsafe and noisy.
approvedChanges.desiredState: Use durable meaningful milestones plus labeled ephemeral phase, sanitized activity, observed time, lease freshness, and bounded progress. Ephemeral data may disappear and cannot satisfy quality.
approvedChanges.rationale: Hybrid signals provide honest liveness without new truth.
approvedChanges.userImpact: Useful live worker status without private internals.
approvedChanges.routeRationale: Needs schema, instrumentation, freshness, redaction, and tests.
approvedChanges.expectedBehavior: Live activity degrades honestly to stale/last-known while durable history remains.
approvedChanges.regressionPlan: Test allowlists, bounds, redaction, expiry, restart, fallback, and authority isolation.
approvedChanges.safetyBoundary: Boundary between append-only semantic trace truth and non-authoritative ephemeral runtime observation.
failureModes: ephemeral telemetry treated as completion evidence
approvedChanges.negativeTestPlan: Reject forbidden fields and oversized payloads; expire stale observations; prove restart loss, durable fallback, no trace append, and no effect on quality exit.
approvedChanges.compatibilityImpact: Existing trace schemas remain authoritative; consumers without telemetry retain durable worker state and existing views.

approvedChanges.question: CHG-human-readable-activity-feed
approvedChanges.currentState: Dry event vocabulary forces users to understand internal ids and schemas to know what happened and what comes next.
approvedChanges.desiredState: Build deterministic source-backed narration where meaningful items identify work/actor, action, outcome, impact, next action, timestamp, freshness, and evidence. Resolve friendly labels and coalesce noise without speculation.
approvedChanges.rationale: Trace truth is optimized for replay, not comprehension.
approvedChanges.routeRationale: Needs fact model, templates, projection, UI, and tests.
approvedChanges.recommendationRationale: User explicitly requested and approved narrative feed.
approvedChanges.expectedBehavior: Meaningful feed items stay concise, contextual, evidence-linked, and trustworthy.
approvedChanges.regressionPlan: Golden fixtures test enrichment, labels, coalescing, missing context, freshness, blockers, route-back, and completion.
approvedChanges.currentPain: Raw claim and evidence event names do not explain progress, significance, blockers, or next action.
approvedChanges.desiredOutcome: At all times the feed explains what happened, why it matters, and what comes next in plain operational language.
approvedChanges.successSignal: Golden narratives cover all loops, worker states, checks, blockers, route-backs, aggregation, stale/live states, and missing context without unsupported claims.
nonGoals: no raw logs in Activity Feed
no fabricated percentage or timing precision

approvedChanges.question: CHG-bounded-developer-log
approvedChanges.currentState: Narrative feed hides execution noise, but maintainers lack a correlated record of externally observable actions. Semantic traces are unsuitable for raw diagnostics.
approvedChanges.desiredState: Add Dev Log capturing permitted worker/session, turn, tool, file-path, command, check, quality, runtime, retry/error, trace-operation, collection, and integration actions with correlation, timing, status, sanitized bounded summaries, refs, and redaction metadata. Store under runtime temp while active/blocked/failed; stream live; restrict permissions; clean after successful closure; grant zero semantic authority.
approvedChanges.rationale: Separate bounded diagnostics gives developers depth without polluting traces or normal feed.
approvedChanges.userImpact: Normal feed stays clear while developer diagnosis is precise.
approvedChanges.maintainerImpact: Adds diagnostic schema, sink, retention, and security duties.
approvedChanges.routeRationale: Security-sensitive cross-cutting implementation requires staged tasks.
approvedChanges.recommendationRationale: User approved bounded Dev Log with explicit safety limits.

agentAssessment.rationale: Redaction and bounded retention make telemetry acceptable.

approvedChanges.expectedBehavior: Developers inspect every permitted observable action during active or failed work; successful closure retains semantic evidence and deletes raw diagnostics.
approvedChanges.regressionPlan: Test event ordering/coverage, correlation, permissions, redaction, allowlists, caps/rotation, live stream, retention, cleanup, forbidden data, and semantic isolation.
approvedChanges.safetyBoundary: Project-local diagnostic telemetry boundary across Pi host events, runtime temp storage, loopback dashboard transport, and successful-close cleanup.
failureModes: unbounded disk or browser memory growth
diagnostic data treated as semantic evidence
approvedChanges.negativeTestPlan: Inject credentials, headers, prompts, reasoning-like fields, source payloads, huge output, malformed correlation, traversal paths, permission failures, and cleanup failures; verify pre-write rejection/redaction, caps, isolation, and zero quality influence.
approvedChanges.compatibilityImpact: Dev Log is additive and optional; existing traces, Activity Feed, loop outputs, and dashboard state remain usable when diagnostics are unavailable.

qualityStandards.description: Decision loop output has at least one Decision and stable Decision ids.
Decisions provide current state, desired state, and rationale fields for the user intention.
Decisions explain how the intention benefits users or improves user outcomes.
Decisions expose maintainer impact and a bounded effort estimate for later semantic cost review.
Decisions classify work scale and choose micro or standard planning before planning handoff.
Decisions choose an explicit next loop; direct implementation is limited to low-risk scoped work with validation.
The agent gives a clear approve/reject/defer/ask-user recommendation and explains why Decisions should proceed.
The agent records its judgment that the user's intention is aligned with real user value and project interests.
Independent judge verifies the decision intent is specific, coherent, and sufficient for planning rather than fluent but vague.
Independent judge verifies effort, maintainer impact, work scale, and desired outcome form a plausible cost tradeoff.
Independent judge verifies declared risk tier and route are plausible for the affected scope and authority needs.
High-risk Decisions have explicit user approval authority and a canonical approval ref.
Current state is grounded in canonical source, KB, trace, Git, digest, or test refs.
Decision evidence is sufficient for planning to trust the intention, including stronger proof for high-risk Decisions.
Decisions declare a valid risk tier; high-risk intentions identify affected layers and alternatives before implementation work is planned.
Decisions do not conflict with active trace goals unless the conflict is resolved.
Knowledge impact is recorded as updated refs or explicit no-impact rationale.
Decisions classify the decision kind so kind-specific quality can apply inside the decision loop.
Hardening decisions define the safety boundary, failure modes, negative tests, and compatibility impact.
Improvement decisions describe current pain, desired outcome, success signal, and non-goals.

qualityStandards.description: Every Decision ref is covered by a Task or explicit resolution.
Each Task has enough bounded context to be assigned to one implementation worker.
Each Task breaks Decision intent into concrete technical requirements.
Each Task has stable acceptance criteria and verification refs or commands.
Each Task declares standard or micro planning depth; micro-plans stay dependency-free and cover one Decision.
Each Task declares worker profile and agent judgment that it is independent and implementation-ready.
Independent judge verifies each Task is atomic enough for one implementation worker and is not a disguised Sprint.
Independent judge verifies acceptance criteria and verification commands are concrete enough to prove implementation completion.
Independent judge verifies path scopes and dependencies are no broader than needed for the Decisions.
No unresolved planning uncertainty remains; decision or user authority is routed instead of leaking into implementation.
Each Task is neither Sprint-sized nor tiny busywork; the Sprint remains the Decision bundle.
Component refs, path scopes, and verification refs align with source ownership contracts.
Dependencies are known, acyclic, and order overlapping work before implementation.
Recurring, triggered, or hook-based work has a complete planned trigger before runtime can start runs from it.
Planning resolutions use a known kind, carry required evidence, and route-back resolutions return to decision authority before implementation.
Planning refs are canonical trace, KB, Git, digest, source, or test refs.

routePlan.rationale: Planning produced worker-ready implementation work units.

qualityStandards.description: Every planned work ref is covered by implementation evidence and no unknown planning refs are introduced.
Implementation changes stay inside planned component/path scope and existing repo paths.
Every planned acceptance criterion is covered by structured evidence refs.
Required implementation checks are structured, present, passing, cover planned verification, and package changes include pack verification.
Required red/green TDD evidence is mapped to planned acceptance criteria.
Implementation output has change-level and aggregate content proof when required.
Worker-produced evidence is tied to active runtime claims and completed worker results.
Changed source/test paths align with OKF source ownership and test coverage.
Agent assessment records maintainability, simplicity, project style, and error-handling readiness.
Completed implementation output has a post-commit archive disposition when retention policy requires cleanup.
CodeWiki-owned review evidence has no blocking diagnostics and links acceptance criteria to concrete evidence.
Independent judge verifies implementation evidence actually supports the claimed changes and acceptance criteria.
Independent judge verifies passing checks are relevant to changed behavior rather than generic or unrelated proof.
Independent judge verifies the production-readiness assessment is specific and not hand-wavy.
No unresolved implementation uncertainty remains; planning, decision, or user authority is routed instead of drifting.
Security/privacy-sensitive changes include explicit review evidence.
UI/page changes include accessibility review evidence.
Dependency-surface changes include risk review evidence.
Release, publication, destructive, or externally visible implementation refs require explicit user approval.
Implementation refs are canonical trace, KB, Git, digest, source, or test refs.
